<reason>B won the confounding clash that decided the motion. A insisted raw averages must include prior breakup and donor routes, but B showed that blames two mothers for a divorce from a prior straight union and for poverty/instability that also harms straight families. Once stable-to-stable is accepted as the causal test, A's sex-complementarity claim had no controlled deficit left, while B's policy remedy - stability via marriage, joint adoption, custody - directly answered A's rescue-vs-equality point.</reason>
